subquestion: Q2: estimate the conduction probabilities at the four specified A-material volume fractions
target_claim: Bound each requested conduction probability reproducibly from the exact single-A periodic crossing event and report the corresponding failure-probability order of magnitude.

leakage_risks: reusing final confirmation seeds during model selection
data_audit.missingness_notes: The problem supplies a stochastic placement mechanism but no sample size; sample size will be determined by interval precision.

baseline.name: center-point random geometric graph
baseline.reason: Provides a cheap comparator and exposes the contribution of rod orientation and finite length.
baseline.implementation: Replace each rod by a center point with an effective connection radius and estimate percolation by simulation.
baseline.validation: Compare probability and monotonic ordering with the continuous-rod model; do not use for final claims.

candidates.name: analytic periodic-bridge probability bound
candidates.formulation: Derive the exact probability that one isotropically oriented flat cylinder crosses the periodic X boundary and use 1-(1-q_A)^N as a rigorous conduction lower bound without sampling error.
assumptions: Rod centers are spatially uniform and independent.
Rod orientations are isotropic on the sphere.
The periodic cube removes edge-density bias.
Samples are independent within each reported estimate.
validation_plan: derive E|u_x|=1/2 and E sqrt(1-u_x^2)=pi/4 from the uniform-sphere marginal
check particle-count rounding against achieved volume fractions
recompute failure probabilities in log space to avoid underflow
refutation_evidence: the assumed center distribution is not uniform or orientations are not isotropic
the direct-crossing event does not produce a left-right path under the official clipping rule
expected_failure_modes: rod-count rounding alters nominal volume fraction
floating-point underflow when reporting failure probability
distributional assumptions do not match the intended random generator
candidates.decision_reason: It preserves the stated geometry and stochastic mechanism while making uncertainty and convergence explicit.

candidates.name: continuous-rod Monte Carlo with periodic cell lists
candidates.formulation: Use the identical random mechanism and exact geometry kernel, but enumerate candidate interactions through a periodic uniform cell list rather than the primary spatial index.
assumptions: The same spatially uniform, isotropic and independent placement model as the primary candidate.
validation_plan: match all-pairs graphs on small cases
match primary estimates under common samples
audit neighbor-cell reach from rod length and threshold
refutation_evidence: cell list omits a pair accepted by all-pairs distance
probability differs under identical generated configurations
expected_failure_modes: long rods span more cells than assumed
candidates.decision_reason: It retains the scientific model but replaces the most implementation-sensitive acceleration component.

candidates.name: deterministic mean-field percolation threshold
candidates.formulation: Approximate conduction from expected neighbor degree alone.
assumptions: Local degree determines spanning probability without finite-size or orientation effects.
refutation_evidence: finite-box Monte Carlo departs from mean-field response
rejection_evidence: The question asks probabilities in a finite periodic cube; expected degree alone cannot identify spanning probabilities or their uncertainty.
candidates.decision_reason: Useful only as a rough plausibility check, not as the requested estimator.

fallback_model: continuous-rod Monte Carlo with periodic cell lists
stop_conditions: the official random-position or orientation distribution differs from uniform/isotropic
the periodic clipping rule is clarified to disconnect the two portions of one crossing object
particle-count rounding cannot be reconciled with the requested fractions

team_approval.record_reason: run-scoped authorization reused for final plan alignment after adversarial review
